quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #9
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: What can you do when your driver license expires?

options.text: Drive during a 90-day grace period.
Drive as long as a licensed driver is with you.
Renew your license within one year after it expires, but you cannot drive with an expired license.
Drive to and from work only.

questions.correctAnswerText: Renew your license within one year after it expires, but you cannot drive with an expired license.
questions.explanation: Your license is void when it expires. There is no grace period. You can renew it within one year of the expiration date, but you cannot drive with an expired license.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a flashing yellow light?

options.text: Speed up.
Come to a complete stop.
Turn on your headlights.
Slow down and drive carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and drive carefully.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light warns you of a hazard. Slow down and drive carefully.

questions.question: How should you enter a freeway?

options.text: Signal, let other traffic go first, and enter at the same speed as traffic.
Signal and enter. Freeway traffic must let you in.
Drive slowly so you can check traffic.
Always stop completely first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, let other traffic go first, and enter at the same speed as traffic.
questions.explanation: Signal and enter at the same speed as traffic. Always let other traffic go first when entering a roadway.

questions.question: What is the best way to handle a tailgater?

options.text: Speed up to increase distance between you and them.
Slam on your brakes to make them back off.
Change lanes or slow down gradually to let them pass.
Ignore them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes or slow down gradually to let them pass.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often to see if someone is tailgating you. If they are, slow down and let them pass. Most rear-end crashes happen because drivers follow too closely.

questions.question: You come to a flashing red light at an intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Stop completely and go when it is safe.
Stop only if other cars are coming.
Stop only if other cars are already in the intersection.
Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely and go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. You must stop, let other traffic go first, and go only when it is safe.

questions.question: You turn onto a two-lane road with a broken yellow line in the middle. What does this tell you?

options.text: Traffic flows in both directions.
Traffic flows in one direction only.
The road is being repaired.
You must stay to the left of the broken yellow lines.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic flows in both directions.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. A broken yellow line can be crossed to pass slower traffic when it is safe.

questions.question: What lights should you use when driving in rain?

options.text: Low beam headlights.
High beam headlights.
Parking lights.
No lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use your low beam headlights when driving in rain.

questions.question: A traffic light turns yellow as you approach an intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up to get through before the red light.
Brake hard to stop.
Be ready to stop in the middle of the intersection.
Be ready to stop before the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop before the intersection.
questions.explanation: A yellow light means the red light is coming soon. Be ready to stop before you reach the intersection.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a railroad crossing warning sign?

options.text: Try to drive faster than a train.
Be ready to stop if a train is near.
Look for a way around any closed gates.
Assume no trains are nearby and drive normally.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop if a train is near.
questions.explanation: Railroad crossing warning signs alert you that a train may be coming. Obey all warning signs and never go around barriers.

questions.question: How can you avoid hitting vehicles in your blind spots?

options.text: Turn your head quickly to check your blind spot before changing lanes.
Adjust your rearview mirrors every few minutes.
Honk your horn right before turning or changing lanes.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head quickly to check your blind spot before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Before turning or changing lanes, turn your head and look over your shoulder in that direction to check your blind spot. Do not rely only on your mirrors.

questions.question: Which statement about railroad crossings is true?

options.text: It is illegal to drive around lowered gates at a crossing.
You must stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger tells you to.
Not all railroad crossings have flashing red signals or gates.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: You must stop at railroad crossings when directed by a flagger, stop sign, or warning devices like gates or flashing lights. Not all crossings have these devices. It is illegal to drive around lowered railroad crossing gates.

questions.question: The best way to avoid hydroplaning is to:

options.text: Keep your tires in good condition.
Slow down when roads are wet or slushy.
Watch for standing water or puddles.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: On wet roads, your car takes longer to stop and may skid during quick turns. Do not use cruise control in wet or icy conditions. Reduce your speed and drive carefully.

questions.question: A driver entering an interstate from an entrance or acceleration ramp:

options.text: Should yield to drivers already on the interstate.
Has the right-of-way.
May force their way into traffic.
Can assume other drivers will change lanes for them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should yield to drivers already on the interstate.
questions.explanation: When entering an interstate from a ramp, you must yield to drivers already on the highway. Merge safely into traffic when it is possible to do so.

questions.question: What does a flashing yellow traffic light mean?

options.text: Merging traffic
Proceed with caution.
Pedestrian crossing
Come to a full stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Proceed with caution.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means you should drive carefully and be ready to stop.

questions.question: What does an orange-colored sign indicate?

options.text: The start of a no passing zone.
A railroad crossing is ahead.
A school zone is ahead.
Construction work is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Construction work is ahead.
questions.explanation: Orange signs with black symbols warn of construction, maintenance, and emergency work.

questions.question: A double solid yellow line down the center of a two-lane road means:

options.text: Traffic moves in opposite directions and drivers cannot pass.
Traffic moves in opposite directions and drivers can pass when safe.
Traffic moves in the same direction and drivers cannot pass.
Traffic moves in the same direction and drivers can pass when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moves in opposite directions and drivers cannot pass.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. Solid lines mean drivers cannot pass.

questions.question: You may cross solid yellow lines:

options.text: To pass traffic moving in the same direction.
During daylight hours only.
At any time.
When making turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: When making turns.
questions.explanation: Broken lines can be crossed, but solid lines cannot. You may cross a solid yellow line only when turning.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: You must travel at the posted speed.
The maximum legal speed is 55 mph.
You must drive 55 mph through the intersection.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum legal speed is 55 mph.
questions.explanation: This is a speed limit sign showing the highest legal speed on that road. In rain, snow, ice, or poor conditions, you may need to drive slower than the posted limit.

questions.question: Larger vehicles have:

options.text: Larger blind spots.
Smaller blind spots.
No blind spots.
The same blind spots as smaller vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Larger blind spots.
questions.explanation: Larger vehicles have larger blind spots. Large trucks and SUVs have areas near the rear that cannot be seen in side or rearview mirrors.

questions.question: To safely pass a bicycle, you should:

options.text: Honk to let the bicyclist know you are passing.
Drive in the bicycle lane until you can pass.
Slow down and give them as much space as possible.
Speed ahead and pull in front of them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and give them as much space as possible.
questions.explanation: Slow down and give bicyclists plenty of space. Bicyclists have less protection than car drivers. Passing too quickly can cause them to lose control.

questions.question: You are driving out of your driveway. What must you do?

options.text: Come to a complete stop before crossing the sidewalk.
Slow down before crossing the sidewalk.
You have the right-of-way over pedestrians on the sidewalk.
You can cross the sidewalk without stopping if you honk first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop before crossing the sidewalk.
questions.explanation: When driving out of a driveway, always stop completely before entering the road. Stop before crossing the sidewalk area. It is against the law not to stop.

questions.question: Two vehicles arrive at an intersection at the same time with no traffic signs or signals. Who has the right-of-way?

options.text: The car coming from the right.
The car coming from the left.
The car whose driver honks first.
The car traveling fastest.

questions.correctAnswerText: The car coming from the right.
questions.explanation: At an intersection of two equal roads with no traffic control, you must yield to the vehicle coming from the right.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: You are entering a one-way street the wrong way.
School crossing ahead.
Do not drive in this lane.
Drivers turning left on green must yield to oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers turning left on green must yield to oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: This sign is placed at traffic signals. It tells drivers that left-turning traffic does not have the right-of-way and must wait for oncoming traffic to clear.

questions.question: Which statement about alcohol is false?

options.text: Your reflexes and reaction time slow down.
Your judgment of speed and distance becomes unclear.
You become less alert.
You calm down and concentrate better.

questions.correctAnswerText: You calm down and concentrate better.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your reaction time, makes it harder to see clearly, affects your judgment of speed and distances, and reduces your ability to recover from headlight glare. It also makes you more likely to take risks.

questions.question: What should you do on slippery roads?

options.text: Slow down.
Drive faster.
Drive at the speed limit with caution.
Never drive faster than 20 mph.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Slow down when rain, snow, or sleet appears. These create slippery conditions. When road conditions are poor, you may need to drive slower than the posted speed limit for safety.

questions.question: What does a steady green light mean?

options.text: You must slow down and be ready to stop.
You must stop and look both ways before going.
You can drive through if the road is clear.
You cannot turn right.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can drive through if the road is clear.
questions.explanation: A steady green light means you may drive through the intersection if it is clear. You may turn right or left unless a sign says you cannot. When turning, yield to other vehicles and pedestrians in the intersection.

questions.question: What does this sign warn drivers about?

options.text: The right lane ends and traffic must merge left.
The road curves ahead.
An intersection is coming.
Road construction ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right lane ends and traffic must merge left.
questions.explanation: This sign means the right lane on the road will end. Traffic in the right lane must move to the left.

questions.question: Which light means you should slow down and be careful at an intersection?

options.text: A flashing yellow light.
A flashing red light.
A solid yellow light.
A solid red light.

questions.correctAnswerText: A flashing yellow light.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down, proceed carefully, and be ready to stop.

questions.question: Distracted driving is:

options.text: Very uncommon.
Extremely dangerous.
Not a concern.
No more risky than regular driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Extremely dangerous.
questions.explanation: Distracted driving is extremely dangerous. It puts you, your passengers, pedestrians, cyclists, and other drivers at risk. Staying focused on the road helps prevent crashes.

questions.question: It starts to rain while you are driving. What should you do?

options.text: Drive faster than other vehicles.
Drive at the posted speed limit.
Slow down.
Drive very close to the vehicle ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: When rain makes it hard to see, reduce your speed. Turn on your headlights so others can see you. If rain is very heavy and you cannot see clearly, pull to the shoulder and stop until it improves.
